claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0007 accurately represents the condition and requirement of 42 U.S.C. 9910(a)(1) governing private nonprofit entities seeking eligible entity status under section 9902(1), correctly retaining the governing condition, the mandatory administration through a tripartite board, and its full participation duties.

Claim C0008 faithfully captures the detailed selection, tripartite composition ratios (1/3 public officials, not fewer than 1/3 low-income representatives, remainder community interests), the appointive official exception, and the residency requirement. However, it completely omits the governing prerequisite lead-in from subsection (a)(1) ('In order for a private, nonprofit entity to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title'), converting a conditional qualification into an overbroad unconditional mandate.

Claim C0009 fully and accurately captures the requirements for public organizations under 42 U.S.C. 9910(b), including the governing condition to qualify as an eligible entity under section 9902(1) and the disjunctive choice between a tripartite board meeting low-income representation and participation standards or an alternative State-specified mechanism.

unit_judgments.rationale: The requirement that a private nonprofit entity administer the CSBG program through a tripartite board that fully participates in development, planning, implementation, and evaluation to be considered an eligible entity is fully covered by C0007.

C0008 states that board members shall be selected by the entity, but omits the governing prerequisite lead-in from subsection (a)(1) governing private nonprofit entities seeking eligible entity status under section 9902(1).
C0008 captures the one-third elected public official composition requirement, but lacks the governing scope qualification from subsection (a)(1).

C0008 correctly retains the exception permitting appointive public officials when fewer than one-third elected officials are reasonably available and willing, but the linked claim omits the governing scope lead-in.

C0008 includes the requirement that not fewer than one-third of the members be democratically chosen representatives of low-income individuals and families, but fails to include the governing scope prerequisite.
C0008 retains the requirement that representatives of low-income individuals and families reside in the neighborhood represented, but inherits the overbroad scope error of the claim.

C0008 includes the requirement that the remainder of the board be officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, law enforcement, education, or other major community groups, but lacks the governing scope condition.
C0009 fully covers the condition that a public organization administer the program through either a tripartite board or another State-specified mechanism to be considered an eligible entity.
C0009 completely incorporates the public organization tripartite board alternative, including democratic selection, low-income representation, residency, and active participation requirements.
C0009 fully retains the alternative permitting administration through another State-specified mechanism assuring decisionmaking and participation by low-income individuals.
